acceptance: For each of the three detectors: a test that reproduces the silent no-op (no posted status / publish skipped after green gate / zero shards or cells) and asserts failure, and a positive test asserting it stays green in the normal case
A live demonstration of detector (1) on a canary PR: removing one secret mapping on a throwaway branch makes the caller job red (revert after)
Detector (2) would have failed run 41949185392 attempt 2 (show the evaluated condition against that run's job results)
No detector can be bypassed by a skipped upstream job (explicit result checks, not implicit success())
context: Member of batch release-v2-remediation. If the detector belongs in Theseus (joeharris76/theseus), make the change there via its own PR, then bump the pin per rv2r-07. GUARDRAILS: detectors only add failure conditions; they never relax or skip an existing check. DECISION GATE: any change that needs repository or environment settings (secrets, rulesets, required checks) goes to the owner.
description: Two outages were silent no-ops reported as green: after #3942 the oracle-verdict caller ran without secrets, posted nothing and its jobs still went green; after #3947 the release run concluded success with publish skipped. Add fail-closed detectors: (1) the BenchBox oracle-verdict and oracle-gate callers end with a job that fails when no verdict or gate status was posted for the head (or the Theseus workflow exposes an output that the caller asserts); (2) release-v2 fails the run when publish did not run after a green gate on a tag target, and fails release-uat when zero shard directories or zero executed cells were found; (3) trunk UAT (rv2r-02) fails when zero cells executed. Each detector has a negative test proving it turns red.
